newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Blasts, accidents mar Philippine New Year revelry.
newsitem.headline: Blasts, accidents mar Philippine New Year revelry.

text.p: At least 10 people were killed and more than 300 injured by fireworks, in road accidents or fights during New Year festivities in the Philippines, police and hospital workers said on Wednesday.
Authorities said the toll was significantly lower than in previous years.

A Continental Air Micronesia flight was forced to abort its landing at Manila's international airport at around midnight after thick firecracker smoke drifted over the runway, an air transport official said.
He said the pilot was initially unable to see the runway lights, but successfully landed after a second attempt.

Six people were killed in road accidents, police said. Two people died of gunshot wounds in Manila after an altercation, while one person was killed by a drunken neighbour who complained that the victim was exploding firecrackers too close to his house, they said.
In central Tacloban city one person died from a gunshot wound, but the assailant was still unknown.

In Manila and its surrounding municipalities, about 220 people, including a five-year old boy, were hurt in firecracker accidents, authorities said. Most of those injured were teenagers and eight of them had to have limbs amputated, they said.
The five-year old boy, who was hit in the right side of the head, suffered bruising of the brain and was in an unstable condition in hospital, police said.
Seven people were brought to hospital with gunshot wounds sustained after people fired guns in the air during New Year celebrations.
Police said a four-year old girl was wounded by a stray bullet in suburban Pasay city.
However, Health Secretary Carmencita Reodica told reporters that no one had died in mishaps with firecrackers or had been killed by stray bullets.
Reodica, who has led a nationwide campaign against the use of firecrackers during New Year celebrations, said the injury toll was significantly lower than last year's 800 victims.
"The campaign has been successful ... Our biggest hospitals have reported a 50 to 60 percent reduction in the number of cases this year," she said.

A doctor at the government-run Philippine General Hospital, the country's biggest casualty centre, said there were more doctors and press photographers in the emergency room than victims. All hospitals were on alert on Tuesday night in anticipation of injuries.
Fifty-two cases of blast injuries were reported from provinces around Manila, records from regional police stations showed.
Twenty-eight people were injured in firecracker explosions in central Tacloban city.
In Zamboanga city, two people were wounded by stray bullets. Zamboanga has recorded high injury tolls in past years because of the high concentration of arms in the region.
Gloria Balboa, programme manager of the Disaster Management Unit of the health department, said this year's celebrations were generally peaceful.
A monitoring centre at the Department of Health said 384 people have been injured by firecrackers since December 1.
Fires also broke out at the height of the revelry, with at least eight blazes reported by the Bureau of Fire Protection.
